compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Author the Copy Needs section schema contract at plugins/dso/docs/contracts/copy-needs-section.md.
**Why**: Sets the interoperability boundary between brainstorm (writer, downstream) and preplanning (reader, downstream); without it, no consistent Copy Needs shape exists.
**Scope**:
- IN: schema doc with required item fields (stable_id, type, location, page, validation rule); controlled `page` vocabulary mechanism; schema_version field; markdown layout; validator (script or documented procedure); passing and failing examples
- OUT: brainstorm hook that writes the section (separate story); preplanning auto-creation logic (separate story)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, plugins/dso/docs/contracts/copy-needs-section.md exists with required item fields stable_id, type, location, page, validation rule documented
  ← Satisfies: sc-1 (sc-1: "/dso:brainstorm tags the epic copy-needed and writes a `## Copy Needs` section conforming to the schema")
- When this story is complete, the contract defines a controlled `page` identifier vocabulary or vocabulary-definition mechanism
  ← Satisfies: sc-1
- When this story is complete, a validator accepts a conforming Copy Needs section
  ← Satisfies: sc-1
- When this story is complete, the validator rejects malformed Copy Needs sections (missing required field or unknown page identifier)
  ← Satisfies: sc-1
- When this story is complete, the contract document includes at least one passing example and one failing example with the rejection reason
  ← Satisfies: sc-1
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations
- [Interoperability] This contract is the single source of truth consumed by the brainstorm writer and preplanning reader; changes are breaking.
- [Versioning] schema_version field reserved so future evolution does not silently break consumers.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
